answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-memory-hard compute-proof-work per identity to act as a resilient anchor in the network graph. Each agent must solve unique, non-sequential puzzles, where the verifier treats every valid output like a crystal clear signal that proves actual resource expenditure. While an honest node pays this cost for one identity, an attacker who tries to wander through the protocol to spawn 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, effectively hitting a spiral of exhaustion. Fraud triggers a permanent identity burn and the ledger rejects all duplicate outputs.
